chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، عَن عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ، عَن مُعَمَّرِ بْنِ خَلَّادَ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Mu'mmar ibn Khallad who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: إِنَّ رَجُلًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يُقَالُ لَهُ قَيْسٌ كَانَ يُصَلِّي فَلَمَّا صَلَّى رَكْعَةً أَقْبَلَ أَسْوَدُ فَصَارَ فِي مَوْضِعِ السُّجُودِ فَلَمَّا نَحَى جَبِينَهُ عَنْ مَوْضِعِهِ تَطَوَّقَ الْأَسْوَدُ فِي عُنُقِهِ ثُمَّ أَنْسَابَ فِي قَمِيصِهِ وَذَهَبَ وَلَمْ يَقْطَعْ صَلَاتَهُ وَإِنِّي أَقْبَلْتُ يَوْمًا مِنَ الْفَرْعِ فَحَضَرَتِ الصَّلَاةُ فَנَزَلْتُ فَصِرْتُ إِلَى ثَمَامَةً فَلَمَّا صَلَّيْتُ رَكْعَةً أَقْبَلَ أَفْعَى نَحْوِي فَأَقْبَلْتُ عَلَى صَلَاتِي لَمْ أُخَفِّفْهَا وَلَمْ يَنْتَقُصْ مِنْهَا شَيْءٌ دَنَا مِنِّي ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى الثَّمَامَةِ فَلَمَّا فَرَغْتُ مِنَ صَلَاتِي وَلَمْ أُخَفِّفْ دُعَائِي دَعَوْتُ بَعْضَهُمْ مَعِي فَقُلْتُ دُونَكَ الْأَفْعَى تَحْتَ الثَّمَامَةِ وَمَنْ لَمْ يَخَفْ إِلَّا اللَّهَ كَفَاهُ

translations.en: Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) said: A man from among the companions of Ali (peace be upon him) called Qays was praying. When he had prayed one unit, a large black snake came and was in the place of prostration. When he lowered his forehead from its place, the black snake encircled his neck, then slid into his shirt and went away, and he did not break his prayer. And I returned one day from al-Far' when the time of prayer entered, so I dismounted and proceeded to a Thumama shrub. When I prayed one unit, a snake came towards me. I continued with my prayer, I did not shorten it nor did anything diminish from it. It came near me then returned to the Thumama. When I finished my prayer and did not shorten my supplication, I called some of them with me and said: Behold the snake under the Thumama. And whoever fears none except Allah, then He suffices for him.

en.summary: Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) narrates two accounts of praying in the presence of snakes without breaking the prayer or shortening the ritual. The first involves a companion of Ali (peace be upon him) named Qays, and the second is the Imam's own experience, demonstrating that the presence of a snake does not invalidate the prayer if one remains composed. This hadith is significant in Shia jurisprudence for establishing that minor distractions or natural creatures do not constitute a 'major distraction' (ghaflah) that breaks wudu or prayer, provided the worshipper maintains focus on their devotion.
en.seo_question: Does the presence of a snake during prayer invalidate the salat according to Shia hadith?

key_terms.ثَمَامَةً: A type of panic grass shrub
key_terms.لَمْ أُخَفِّهَا: Did not shorten it (referring to the prayer)
